transcript: Today my boyfriend Paul and I went to see shucked on Broadway, a new musical about corn. I'm not gonna really talk about the plot because I want to support the productions boldly. Cryptic marketing strategy, and I think this show deserves to do really well. All you really need to know is that it's great. And I think part of its charm is how unexpected it is, because you can't really imagine just how good it's gonna be by only seeing that same corn image everywhere. It's a completely original story and score. It's genuinely very funny, and the performances are spectacular. Alex Newell gives a performance that's rightfully going to be talked about for a while. The comedy is a mixture of silly and clever. The music is catchy, and the characters are really engaging. I think what makes the show such a home run and a clear front runner of the season, in my eyes, is how it exemplifies that your musical doesn't need to be about anything groundbreaking or particularly theatrical in order to be really incredible. Shocked proves that good writing, music, casting, and direction are more than enough to grow something wonderful.
